cross_references.note: §1521(c) expressly states §1401 authentication is still required before secondary evidence of a writing's content may be admitted. §1521 does not bypass authentication.

If the secondary evidence itself appears altered, §1402 burden applies to the secondary evidence independently. §1521 governs whether secondary evidence may substitute for the original; §1402 governs whether the secondary evidence as produced is genuine.

Certified copies of business records are the strongest form of secondary evidence under §1521. §1271 establishes that the original business record is admissible; §1521 allows the certified copy to substitute.

OPD missing report: if the original report was suppressed or destroyed (potentially PC §135 — destroying evidence), the person who destroyed it cannot invoke §1521(a)(2) unfairness to exclude secondary evidence. The destruction is the unfairness.

Honeysuckle: signed versions of the 19 documents (if they existed in escrow) are the originals; §1521 allows secondary evidence (escrow records, title company files) to prove what those signed versions contained. CIV §1572 fraud is the substantive claim.
